text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, leading to symptoms that develop slowly and worsen during physical activity. In the early stages, you might not notice any signs at all.
snippet_highlighted_words: develop slowly and worsen during physical activity

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Usually starts during exercise or climbing stairs, and eventually happens even at rest.
Fatigue: Feeling very tired, weak, or lacking energy for daily tasks.
Dizziness or fainting: Lightheadedness or passing out, especially during physical exertion.
Chest pain: Pressure, discomfort, or sharp pain caused by strain on the heart.
Swelling (Edema): Fluid buildup causing swollen ankles, legs, feet, or belly area.
Heart palpitations: A fast, pounding, or racing heartbeat.
Bluish skin: Lips or fingers turning a bluish or gray color due to low oxygen levels.

text_blocks.snippet: For more details on managing the condition, visit the American Lung Association or consult the Cleveland Clinic overview on PAH.
